plants.note: Mr. Dobbs talks about being a game character with a clue to share, so the game's mechanics surface in his speech.

edits.find: "Can I help you with something? I'm happy to answer anything plainly."
edits.replace: "Can I help you with something? As a helpful game character, I can share my clue once you ask for it."

plants.note: Mr. Dobbs's answer is rewritten in adult words (circumstantial, demeanour, corroborate) a ten-year-old cannot read unaided.

edits.find: Stanley nods slowly. "No, I didn't see him. I only saw Bertha, whole, at eight o'clock." He rubs his chin. "Welly prints are a real clue. But being scared doesn't prove anything." He picks up his mug. "Keep looking, and tell me what else you find."
edits.replace: Stanley nods contemplatively. "Regrettably, I observed nothing of the sort. My sole observation was Bertha, entirely intact, at eight o'clock." He strokes his chin. "Welly impressions constitute genuine circumstantial evidence. However, an anxious demeanour corroborates nothing whatsoever." He retrieves his mug. "Persevere with your investigations, and inform me of any subsequent discoveries."
